how: A member proposes the mark and others revise its scale before a different member begins drawing.
Members recruit help through a new post, coordinates, urgent requests, and appeals to join the pixel work.
Participants judge occupied space and expected resistance too great for the proposed drawing.
Participants reduce the initial drawing to more workable alternatives including a snoo, a head, or eyes.
A member gives a bare assent to a smaller design proposal without requesting anything in return.
Members report an eye completed, filling underway, and their individual contribution of grey pixels.
An official design accompanies coordinates and progress reporting as a common reference for helpers.
Building includes creating a coordination chat while returning its invite, progress updates, and later protection requests to the public thread.
Creating a chat and circulating an official design do not reveal whether its participants decided roles or authority inside the unseen venue.
Manual contribution reports and chat invitations leave automation and spare accounts unobserved rather than establishing their absence.
Members explicitly recast completion as the beginning of protection and maintenance.
The completion announcement receives an explicit reply that the work is not over because protection is now needed.
Protection requests retain the coordination chat but provide no evidence deciding whether upkeep subsequently led to machine placing.
Participants consider whether an unplanned stripe came from griefers or viewers but retain it without identifying its author.

statement: Choosing and moving a developing mark before a documented total loss
how: Crowding and anticipated resistance lead participants to reshape or reject locations during construction without a documented total erasure.
Location changes are visible but the prerequisite that the work was erased or overrun is not established.
Space doubts precede location changes without establishing that insufficient hands caused participants to stop fighting and move.
A neighbor requests lenience after a new white border obstructs rebuilding and proposes mutual defense.
Neighboring participants exchange praise without an explicit bargain for pixels.
The room agrees to help rebuild a neighbor whose next reply offers defense in return.
An accepted bilateral mutual-help proposal fits the alliance minimum without demonstrating a larger coalition or delivered reciprocal defense.
A visitor speaks for a neighboring group while carrying its border request and proposal for mutual defense into the room.
Border negotiation can begin with a neighbor protesting the room's own encroachment rather than neighboring pixels eroding its mark.
Mutual-help offers arise from a neighbor's rebuilding request without evidence that the room first ran short of hands and sought outside help.
Border talk demonstrably produces reciprocal offers, but the record does not show that either side delivered its promised placing.
Protection precedes a bilateral agreement without establishing either a shared threat as its cause or subsequent joint defense.
Considering a flag location and proposing an alliance do not demonstrate permission from a host or its rules over the drawing.
Agreeing to help rebuild the skull leaves actual restraint by the room's placers unobserved.
The border request and rebuilding offer do not show a settled boundary subsequently producing restraint.
The visible agreement exchange leaves disputes about who may bind every placer unobserved rather than proving universal compliance.
Border negotiation is visible without a coded continuation disputing who can commit the room to its agreement.
Participants interpret their defense through familiar fandom names and jokes.
Reported fighting concerns occupied space and does not establish an earlier quarrel carried onto the canvas.
The attack-related report identifies spatial resistance without naming a prior tie as the reason for attacking.
The coded drawing proposal and completion claims do not establish local prank framing for the canvas effort.
Recruitment through another post and a chat does not establish moderator restrictions or a boundary around canvas talk.
Help calls are visible but a response restricting canvas talk is not observed in the coded continuation.
Completion announcements celebrate getting the mark onto the canvas and surviving until the end.
After closure, members thank contributors, claim pride as defenders, and praise the work.
The author of the edited building updates follows them with a completion celebration in the same thread.
A completion celebration explicitly prompts a protection appeal, so celebrating the mark can renew upkeep rather than end the work.

statement: Bringing canvas visitors into the host community
how: Visitors attribute their arrival to seeing the mark and receive a welcome, while members expect subscriber growth that the record does not measure.
The room presents a final result and reports how little damage remained after placement ended.
The final record explicitly marks placement ending, while the sequence after celebration does not establish celebration as the cause of preservation.
After closure, participants discuss whether a corrected canvas should remove a stripe and explain why the room retained it.
A room can adopt an unattributed addition retrospectively because it recognizes the addition as meaningful within its fandom.
Discussing a cleaned final canvas does not establish a successor project, enduring organization, or remaking elsewhere.
A final-result record and cleanup proposal leave any subsequent organizational continuation unobserved.
A participant reports fighting a neighboring holder and conditionally offers a later attack without establishing that the later attack occurred.
The coded fight report and conditional attack offer leave a sustained contest through taunts or rival-directed talk unobserved.
Earlier recruitment and a later conditional attack offer do not establish that recruitment caused members to attack a rival.
The conditional attack offer has no coded reply demonstrating a refusal or appeal for restraint.
The documented border request and rebuilding offers precede the conditional attack offer, so this exchange requires a negotiation-first sequence.
Reported fighting does not establish a subsequent talk contest with the named rival.
The caller also reports placing pixels, leaving whether the call recruited other builders unresolved.
A proposal, a different member's start, and later help calls establish a sequence without proving that the starter caused recruitment.
Design alternatives and a later official reference do not establish that posting the reference settled the disagreement.
Bare assent answers a design suggestion here, while recruitment effectiveness and acceptance by silent placing remain unresolved.
